paragraphs.text: This is [red tea](red:definition) from [Yuchi](yuchi:where-it-is), the township that holds Sun Moon Lake in the middle of Nantou County, made in 1979. Red tea took hold here because of the land: a warm, wet basin of mist and cloud, deep reddish soil, and a lake that keeps the weather mild and steady. The Japanese tea men who first trialled it compared it to the Assam country of India, and the [Assam type](yuchi:assam-planting) seed they brought in is still the root of the township's red tea.

The year puts this tea in the township's lean decades. From the 1970s, rising wages made hand picked leaf costly against red tea from other countries, and many growers here moved to oolong or to other crops. The return to local red tea came only after the 1999 earthquake.

Red tea has no tradition of [ageing](red:ageing). It is made to be drunk fresh, and sealed it is expected to keep for about three years at most. At forty-seven years, this leaf has lived far beyond the life the trade gives it.

brewing.text: Red tea takes water near the boil, about 90 to 100°C; hotter water draws out its aroma and flavour more fully, but its bitterness faster too. In a pot or mug, use about a rounded spoon of leaf for each cup and steep three to five minutes, less for broken leaf and a little less, and a little cooler, for a light, delicate tea. Left too long, it turns bitter and drying, because time and heat pull more tannins from the leaf.

notice.text: A sweet cup, often with honey, floral or fruity notes, malt in many, and a brisk strength in the stronger teas. The liquor runs red, bright to deep.
